item.title: Seattle police won't reopen Kurt Cobain death case: ‘Case remains closed’
item.description: Social media has been abuzz after dubious new reports that Seattle grunge icon Kurt Cobain did not die by suicide, but was murdered in 1994 — but Seattle police say the “case remains closed."

item.title: Seattle weather: More isolated rain, snow in western WA
item.description: Today, we expect an isolated rain-snow mix at times, but daytime accumulations are unlikely with a better chance of sticking where it falls tonight.

item.title: Convicted sex trafficker arrested on domestic violence charges in Bellevue, WA
item.description: Reginald Irvin, a convicted sex trafficker sentenced in 2013, is back behind bars on new charges.

item.title: Seattle Seahawks fan who lost signed football meets Josh Jobe, visits VMAC
item.description: An 8-year-old Seattle Seahawks fan who lost his signed football at the championship parade received a new one from cornerback Josh Jobe, along with a signed jersey and tour of the VMAC.

item.title: Who could buy the Seattle Seahawks as franchise could sell for $8B
item.description: The Seattle Seahawks are officially up for sale and could fetch a record $8 billion. Here’s a look at potential buyers, from Jeff Bezos and Bill Gates to Steve Ballmer and other billionaires.

item.title: Washington State Ferries to charge 3% fee on card payments March 1
item.description: Starting March 1, a mandatory 3% fee will be added to all Washington State Ferries fares purchased with a credit or debit card.

item.title: I-405 construction in Bothell, WA to cause four weeks of road closures
item.description: Drivers are in for several weekends of road closures along I-405 and State Route 522 in Bothell.

item.title: Lynnwood, WA officials could terminate contract with license plate reader vendor
item.description: The Lynnwood City Council is considering ending its contract with Flock Safety’s license plate reader cameras over privacy concerns and data access by immigration agents.

item.title: Seattle's first homicide of 2026 is a case that began more than 50 years ago
item.description: In 1973, a 19-year-old man was shot near Garfield High School, a tragedy that left him paralyzed for the rest of his life. The medical examiner has now officially ruled his recent death a homicide.

item.title: Bellingham, WA cold weather shelters open due to dangerously cold temps
item.description: Shelter operators in Whatcom County say that temps fell Tuesday to dangerous levels, and they expected more bitter cold to settle in on Wednesday night.
